title: Charity OS provider landscape
method: AI-assisted review of official documentation, source repositories and public GitHub metadata. Stripe Directory was attempted by the root agent with the official current CLI but rejected its user agent; authoritative web fallback was used. This is a bounded planning sample, not a complete market census or product endorsement.
maintenance_note: GitHub default-branch commits and pushed_at are dated observations only. A push may be a branch or automation update and does not establish a supported production release. UTC commit dates are preserved.

status_vocabulary.documented: Explicitly described by a source read for this review; not independently tested.
status_vocabulary.code-observed: Source file/tree inspected; supported product contract not established.
status_vocabulary.unverified: No adequate evidence checked; does not mean the feature is absent.

providers.name: CiviCRM
providers.model: Open source; self-hosted or separately hosted
providers.license: AGPL-3.0 (repository metadata; inspect the selected distribution and extensions before reuse)
providers.api: APIv4 exposes entity actions; action coverage varies. The documented default validates the logged-in user permissions. Test the exact entities, ACLs and release before connecting.
providers.access: CMS roles plus native CiviCRM ACLs can limit components, contact groups, custom fields and events. Broad view-all rights override some granular restrictions.
providers.tenancy: The sources checked describe permissions inside an installation. An isolated multi-organization Charitology hosting boundary was not verified; do not equate ACL groups with tenants.
providers.export: Contact/component CSV exports support field selection and reusable mappings. A successful full export/restore including files and extensions was not tested.
providers.cost: Downloadable code has no license fee. Hosting, implementation, security updates, mail transport and support need budgets. Spark has separate hosted plans and feature limits; current quotes must be checked.
limits: Install and patch a supported release; the official advisory page records API permission fixes in August 2026. No security clearance is claimed.
The component list does not establish a full nonprofit accounting ledger or restricted-fund compliance.
No Charitology connector has been built or tested.
providers.reuse: Evaluate as a separate donor/member CRM and consent system connected to Charitology through a narrow service account.

providers.name: ERPNext and Frappe
providers.model: Open source; self-hosted or Frappe Cloud
providers.license: ERPNext GPL-3.0; archived non_profit GPL-3.0; check other apps separately

maintenance.description: Free and Open Source Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP)

capabilities: ERP core with accounting, assets, stock, buying, selling and projects
Role, document and field permission controls
providers.api: Frappe generates REST interfaces for DocTypes and supports token/session authentication. API access must use a constrained user and versioned mappings.
providers.access: Roles control DocType operations; permission levels can restrict groups of fields, and user permissions can constrain linked records.
providers.tenancy: Frappe documents one database per site, with each site a tenant. Shared hosts and operators still require deployment controls and isolation tests.
providers.export: Data Export selects DocType, fields and filters and outputs CSV/Excel. Site backup/restore and all attachments need a separate pilot test.
providers.cost: Open-source code; hosting, administration, implementation and support remain costs. No current managed-hosting quote was verified.
limits: frappe/non_profit was archived July 31, 2025. Its observed default-branch commit is June 12, 2024. The repository points to v14 documentation.
The nonprofit marketing page still advertises donation, grant and volunteer features; this is not evidence that the archived addon supports current ERPNext.
Do not install the archived addon as the default foundation without a maintained fork, compatibility tests and an owner for updates.
providers.reuse: Evaluate current ERPNext accounting/operations independently of the archived nonprofit addon. Prototype missing nonprofit workflows as a separate maintained Frappe app only after fit testing.

providers.name: Tendenci
providers.model: Open source; self-hosted with separately offered hosting/services
providers.license: GPL-3.0-or-later stated in README and LICENSE; GitHub automatic license detection returns NOASSERTION

maintenance.description: Tendenci - The Open Source Association Management System (AMS)

capabilities: Chapter membership import, search, export and invoices
providers.api: Documented Django REST Framework API is read-only and limited to entities, events, memberships, users and groups. It must be enabled; API keys travel in the Authorization header.
providers.access: Chapter leaders can manage their own chapter memberships while administrators can manage all. This is a documented scoped workflow, not a full security audit.
providers.tenancy: Chapter scope is documented. Hard tenant isolation between unrelated organizations was not verified.
providers.export: Chapter membership export/import is documented. Whole-site restore and preservation of every relationship/file were not tested.
providers.cost: Code is open source. Self-hosting needs a server and administration; current hosted plan pricing was not checked.
limits: Read-only API limits synchronization; write integration would require extension or another supported interface.
Association workflows are not a substitute for program outcomes, grant accounting or sensitive case-management controls.
No independent accessibility, restore or permission test was performed.
providers.reuse: Evaluate for membership-led organizations and chapters; link through exports or the documented read API before considering a write connector.

providers.name: Odoo Community and OCA association addons
providers.model: Community self-hosting; proprietary Enterprise/Online plans are separate
providers.license: Odoo Community LGPL-3.0; OCA repositories AGPL-3.0 with per-module manifest licenses; Enterprise is a separate commercial license

maintenance.description: Odoo addons for membership related tasks
Odoo for NGO's and humanitarian organization

capabilities: OCA 19.0 membership, delegated membership, variable periods and website member directory addons
OCA 18.0 has a different migration/feature set
Model access rights, record rules and restricted fields
providers.api: External API documentation states Odoo Online API access requires the Custom plan; do not assume a Standard subscription includes it. Selected self-hosted version/protocol and module compatibility need testing.
providers.access: Groups grant model operations. Record rules filter records after model checks and default to allow when no applicable rule restricts access; configure and test every boundary.
providers.tenancy: Multi-company or membership groups must not be presumed equivalent to isolated Charitology organizations. Separate-database deployment and operational boundaries need evaluation.
providers.export: Official import/export docs cover CSV/Excel and stable External IDs for updates. A complete migration of custom modules, files and permissions was not tested.
providers.cost: Community code has no software license fee; hosting, migration, addon support and implementation are separate. Enterprise/Online terms and API plan costs require a current quote.
limits: OCA/vertical-ngo 18.0 and default 19.0 had repository scaffolding but no addon directories in the observed trees. Do not market them as a ready NGO suite.
OCA/vertical-association has real addons, but migration coverage differs by branch; never promise all modules across all Odoo versions.
The observed Odoo default branch is not a recommendation to deploy that branch. Select a supported release with matching modules.
providers.reuse: Evaluate for organizations with broad ERP/membership needs. Prefer API/export integration with a supported deployment over importing OCA code into the MIT Charitology site.

providers.name: OpenProject
providers.model: Open-source Community self-hosting; paid Enterprise cloud/on-premises additions
providers.license: GPL-3.0 repository; compare Enterprise terms before using additions

maintenance.description: OpenProject is the leading open source project management software for product, project and portfolio management. A powerful Jira alternative with agile planning, issue tracking, roadmaps, Gantt charts, time tracking, collaboration features, and more. Available on premises or in the cloud. ⭐ Star us on GitHub

capabilities: Work packages with assignee, status, priority and dates
Project plans, dependencies and Gantt views
providers.api: Hypermedia REST API v3 is documented. Endpoint coverage and authorization must be tested for the connector; an API is not proof every UI operation is supported.
providers.access: Configurable project and global roles govern permissions. Work-package export requires its own permission; external work-package sharing is labeled an Enterprise addon.
providers.tenancy: Project boundaries are documented, not independent tenant isolation. An OS deployment serving unrelated charities requires a separate tenant design.
providers.export: Work-package lists export to CSV/XLS/PDF; single records have PDF/Atom export. XLS does not preserve hierarchy as displayed; export limits and long-text coverage need checking.
providers.cost: Community is free with no minimum users. The current pricing page showed Basic EUR5.95/user/month with a 25-user minimum; locale, hosting and term selection can change the quote.
limits: It is a project tool, not a donor CRM, grants disbursement service or full accounting system.
Feature inclusion differs between Community and Enterprise; compare the selected plan.
No deployment or data restore test was performed.
providers.reuse: Candidate project execution backend or optional connector for teams already using it; preserve stable external IDs and link Charitology observations to work packages.

providers.name: KoboToolbox
providers.category: Field data collection and program evidence
providers.model: Open source; hosted plans or self-hosted deployment
providers.license: KPI server AGPL-3.0; verify other components separately

maintenance.description: kpi is the server for KoboToolbox. It includes an API for users to access data and manage their forms, question library, sharing settings, create reports, and export data.

capabilities: Offline browser forms and Android KoboCollect
Submission review, validation, reports and maps
API data export and external dashboard connections
providers.api: KPI v2 API supports projects, submissions, permissions and exports; v1 endpoints are deprecated. JSON, CSV and XLSX data retrieval is documented.
providers.access: Project sharing permissions distinguish form access and submission actions, including restrictions to submissions by specified users. Test a collector/validator/admin scenario before rollout.
providers.tenancy: Hosted Global and EU servers are documented. Project sharing and account/organization features must be tested against the chosen plan; no isolation audit was conducted.
providers.export: CSV/XLSX synchronous exports and raw JSON are documented. Preserve form version, field definitions and attachment references alongside submissions.
providers.cost: A free Community plan exists; submission, storage and AI-service quotas apply. The pricing page returned 403 during this review, so numeric quotas/prices were not treated as current verified facts.
limits: Offline use needs the form loaded/downloaded before losing connectivity; later sync still requires a network.
This is data collection infrastructure, not by itself a constituent CRM or financial ledger.
Do not collect identifying beneficiary records in the current public/local Charitology OS.
providers.reuse: Strong candidate for an optional field-evidence connector: import authorized aggregate/anonymized observations with form version, source and collection date.
providers.tested: Documentation and repository inspection only; no installation, account purchase, product security audit or end-to-end integration test.

providers.name: OSCaR
providers.model: Open-source private hosting; separately offered hosted subscription
providers.license: README states AGPL without an exact version; GitHub metadata did not identify a license. Confirm the selected distribution license before reuse.

maintenance.description: OSCaR Open Source Case Management and Reporting System

capabilities: Client, family, community and partner records
Assessments, care plans, tasks and case notes
providers.api: The observed repository contains API v1 controllers and request tests. A supported public integration contract and endpoint coverage were not verified.
providers.access: Official feature page describes four permission sets and change logs. Fine-grained isolation, deployment configuration and real-data suitability were not independently tested.
providers.tenancy: Repository and private-hosting guides use organization/tenant concepts. Isolation behavior was not tested.
providers.export: Repository contains export tasks and the product documents reporting/data manipulation. Full, supported portability and restore procedures were not verified.
providers.cost: README describes open-source use and hosted subscription. Current numeric subscription pricing was not established in this review.
limits: At the recorded commit, .ruby-version is 2.3.7 and Gemfile pins Rails 4.2.5. Do not confuse a recent push with a modern runtime or a security review.
Sensitive case data requires a dedicated organizational safety/privacy assessment; the current Charitology OS is unsuitable for it.
Mobile/API support cannot be inferred from controller files alone.
providers.reuse: Study casework data models and practitioner workflows. Do not select this upstream deployment by default without a supported modernization and operational owner.

providers.name: CaseLight
capabilities: Configurable forms, program streams and assessments
Case notes, tasks, documents and shared calendar
Role/field authorization and emergency-access workflow claimed by maintainer
Audit and portability workflows documented by maintainer
providers.api: README says the upstream v1 mobile API was intentionally not carried into its pilot scope. Do not assume the OSCaR connector works with this fork.
providers.access: Maintainer documents MFA, role/field authorization, encryption and audit controls. These are maintainer claims, not an independent assurance or certification.
providers.tenancy: Whole-tenant portability and per-organization controls are described. No tenant-boundary penetration test or production assessment was performed here.
providers.export: Maintainer documents subject-access export and an encrypted tenant portability bundle. Restore-drill evidence exists in the repository; it was not independently rerun.
providers.cost: No software subscription charge was established; infrastructure, patching, administration and production preparation need budgets. No hosted-support quote was checked.
limits: SECURITY.md explicitly limits the evaluation pilot to synthetic/representative data and lists separate production gates.
The production checklist includes retention policy, independent keys, network controls, backups and named incident owners. A polished compliance folder does not establish certification.
Case management is outside the first proposed Charitology shared-operations pilot.
providers.reuse: Run only a synthetic-data evaluation if casework becomes a confirmed need. Reuse its concepts and test cases as references; keep any AGPL-derived implementation separate and license-reviewed.

providers.name: Givebutter
providers.license: No open-source application license verified; integrate through documented interfaces and account terms
capabilities: Events, tickets, auctions and peer-to-peer fundraising
providers.api: Official help describes API keys and public developer access. Webhooks include campaign/contact/transaction/refund events; contact.created explicitly does not fire for CSV imports. Exact endpoints and rate limits need a connector spike.
providers.access: Preset Admin, Finance, Campaign Editor and CRM Manager roles plus campaign scoping and separate mobile permissions are documented.
providers.tenancy: Hosted account boundary; data residency, backup recovery and tenant isolation were not independently assessed.
providers.export: Transaction CSV export is documented. A complete contact/history/consent/attachment round trip was not tested.
providers.cost: Pricing page currently states optional tips enabled: 0% platform fees with a processor-fee guarantee for nonprofits. Tips off: 3% platform fee plus standard processing (cards 2.9% + USD0.30; ACH 1.9% + USD0.30). Plus starts at USD29/month and is contact-tiered; recheck eligibility and channel-specific fees.
limits: Mobile app fees have a separate published treatment; do not generalize the web tip guarantee to every channel.
Do not label fundraising CRM as complete program, case-management or nonprofit accounting functionality.
Provider statement and pricing review are not an independent product test or endorsement.
providers.reuse: Offer an optional external fundraising connector with signed-webhook verification, idempotency and reconciliation/export; keep payment credentials and card data out of Charitology.

providers.name: Salesforce Nonprofit Cloud
providers.category: Hosted nonprofit CRM, fundraising, programs and grantmaking
providers.model: Proprietary hosted platform; nonprofit entitlements and addons vary
providers.license: Commercial subscription; no open-source license for Nonprofit Cloud core was verified
capabilities: Grantmaking opportunities, reviews, budgets and grantee experiences through selected products
providers.api: Salesforce REST access requires both an API-enabled organization/edition and a user with API Enabled permission. Edition, object entitlement and limits need contract-specific verification.
providers.access: API user permissions are documented. This review did not independently test Nonprofit Cloud sharing, permission sets, field security or portal boundaries.
providers.tenancy: Provider-hosted Salesforce organization; chosen residency, tenant controls and backup commitments need procurement review.
providers.export: Data Export produces CSV sets and optional files on edition-dependent schedules. Formula/roll-up fields are excluded; export is not proof of complete metadata/configuration restore.
providers.cost: Canonical U.S. pricing page opened October 25, 2026 showed Core USD70/user/month, Advanced USD125 and Sales/Service Max USD285, billed annually. Eligible nonprofits may receive 10 Core licenses at no cost; eligibility is not established for Charitology. Older indexed regional variants still show USD60/100. Grantmaking has separate product/pricing pages; obtain a written scope/quote.
limits: A discounted license is not an implementation, migration, administrator or support budget.
Do not apply older Nonprofit Success Pack tutorials or older price cards automatically to current Nonprofit Cloud.
Portals, marketing, integrations and usage limits can add distinct entitlements/costs.
providers.reuse: Support organizations that already use Salesforce through scoped export/API adapters. Do not make a commercial platform mandatory for the public Charitology OS.
